submission.natural_language_explanation: Retrospective layer-0 unigram detector: the strength is fixed by which token sits in the current position (97% of the integrated-gradient attribution is on the peak token, token identity explains 96% of scan variance, and a token keeps its strength across carriers), firing at 0.3-2.0 of the 1.46 scan scale on a fixed, idiosyncratic set of English token forms - 'would'/'wouldn' and 'called' (strongest mid-text), the 'roll' stem (roll, rolls, rolled, rolling, roller), 'til'/'till' and weakly 'until', the weekday names Monday-Thursday and Sunday and their truncations (Tues, Mond, Thur, Fri, Sun), the time words tomorrow/tonight/today/noon/midnight/morning, the apostrophe token, the digit tokens 5-9 (strongest on 8-9), and individual capitalised name tokens (Robin, Roy, Joe, Bernie, Hillary, Warren, Cosby) - while staying at or below zero on every month name (January-December), every place name tested (London, Paris, France, China, Italy, Texas), the other modals (will, must, should, may, can, shall, might), the rest of the 'call' paradigm (call, calls, calling), the 'roll' lookalikes (troll, toll, doll, poll, role, rule), most personal names (Robert, James, Kevin, Anna, Sarah) and ordinary or Latinate vocabulary. Independently of token identity a text's first token is boosted by roughly +0.5 to +1.2, so capitalised sentence-openers that read about 0 mid-text (She, They, He, It, We, If, So, That, For, Please, Our, Once) fire at 0.6-1.3 there - which is why most of the scan's top examples peak at index 0 - and the pole prepares no particular upcoming token (Jacobian and logit-lens kurtosis are both ~3.0).

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Our annual audit begins in late September and finishes in early November.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Month names are the hypothesis's clearest stated negatives (every month reads at or below zero); this puts two of them mid-text with no listed trigger anywhere.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The delegation flew from Paris to London before continuing on to Beijing.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Place names are claimed to stay at or below zero, so this tests the claim that the firing set is idiosyncratic rather than geography-like.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: You will need photo identification, and you must arrive at least an hour early.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Contains the other modals 'will' and 'must' in ordinary use, which the hypothesis says do not fire, in contrast with 'would'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Please call the front desk if the room is cold, and they will send someone up.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The rest of the 'call' paradigm (call, calls, calling) is claimed negative while 'called' fires, so this tests whether the effect is really restricted to the one form.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The troll beneath the bridge demanded a toll from every goat that crossed the stream.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The named 'roll' lookalikes troll and toll are claimed to stay at or below zero, testing whether the 'roll' stem claim draws a real boundary.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Robert, James, Kevin, Anna and Sarah shared a taxi to the conference hall.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Several ordinary personal names the hypothesis says do not fire, in a mid-sentence list, testing the claim that only a few idiosyncratic names activate the pole.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He tilted the lamp toward the page so the print was easier to read.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A word containing the 'til' letters in a different morphological family, which a token-form detector is claimed to exclude while 'til' and 'till' fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: It’s been a long day, and we’re all ready to go home.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Contains typographic apostrophes (U+2019) rather than the ASCII apostrophe token that is claimed to fire, testing token identity at the character level.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The storm passed just before dawn. They reopened the road by eight.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A capitalised sentence opener that the hypothesis says reads about zero mid-text, since the boost is claimed to apply only to a text's first token; this opener sits after the first sentence.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The shipment leaves the depot on Friday and reaches the coast the following afternoon.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The hypothesis enumerates Monday-Thursday, Sunday and the truncation Fri but omits Friday itself, so a negative label here tests whether that fixed set is really the full weekday set.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The device was called a hydrofoil by the engineers who first built it.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout for 'called' in a subject-position passive on a new topic, well away from the scan example about the mitochondrion.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Had the switch closed earlier, the relay would have tripped within seconds.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout for 'would' in a counterfactual technical sentence, a genre and construction unlike the political-news scan example.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The backup rotation runs at noon on Wednesday and again at midnight on Sunday.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout for the weekday and time-word claims in an operations-schedule genre, with noon, Wednesday, midnight and Sunday all mid-sentence.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Item 8 shipped on time; item 9 arrived two days late.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout for the standalone digit claim (strongest on 8-9) in a ledger genre, with both digits past the unmeasured first position.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Gently roll the dough flat, then let it rest under a towel.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout for the 'roll' stem in an imperative cooking context, a sense and position different from the scan examples.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The coach said Bernie threw two touchdown passes on Sunday, and the crowd went wild.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout for a listed capitalised name and a weekday in a sports-report genre, with the name placed mid-sentence rather than at the unmeasured first position.
